title: Profiling Application-Specific Properties of Irregular Graph Algorithms on GPUs
problem: Despite sophisticated GPU profiling tools (NVIDIA Nsight Compute/Systems), developers often miss application-specific insights that simple manual profiling techniques can reveal, particularly for irregular workloads like graph algorithms.
motivation: Graph algorithms exhibit highly irregular memory access and control flow patterns. Application-specific profiling via manual counters can expose performance bottlenecks and guide effective optimizations better than generic profiling tools.
method: The researchers added custom monitoring code—called instrumentation—to five high-performance GPU graph analysis programs, rather than relying solely on standard profiling tools like NVIDIA Nsight Compute. They inserted counters tracking two levels: overall GPU statistics and individual measurements from each thread. By analyzing these counters, they could see exactly how the code behaves in practice, verify whether their assumptions were correct, and identify specific parts needing optimization.
key_novelty: Custom instrumentation with global and per-thread counters reveals insights about irregular GPU workloads like graph algorithms that standard profilers cannot.
contributions: Demonstration of manual counter-based profiling on GPU graph algorithms
Uncovering of application-specific behavioral patterns in graph analytics
Performance optimization techniques derived from profiling insights
Best practices for irregular workload profiling on GPUs
limitations: Limited to 5 specific graph algorithms; general applicability to other irregular workloads not explored; reproducibility details not provided in abstract.
